stem:
An electrochemical cell is constructed using two half-cells.

- an $\text{Sn}^{4+}/\text{Sn}^{2+}$ half-cell
- an $\text{Al}^{3+}/\text{Al}$ half-cell

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
State the material used for the electrode in each half-cell.

- $\text{Sn}^{4+}/\text{Sn}^{2+}$ half-cell
- $\text{Al}^{3+}/\text{Al}$ half-cell

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The cell is operated at $298\text{ K}$.

The $\text{Al}^{3+}/\text{Al}$ half-cell has standard concentrations.

The $\text{Sn}^{4+}/\text{Sn}^{2+}$ half-cell has $[\text{Sn}^{4+}] = 0.300\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ and $[\text{Sn}^{2+}] = 0.150\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.
parts.text: Use the Nernst equation to calculate the electrode potential, $E$, of the $\text{Sn}^{4+}/\text{Sn}^{2+}$ half-cell under these conditions.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the overall cell reaction that occurs.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Aluminium is produced industrially by electrolysis of a melt containing large amounts of $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ions.

Calculate the mass of aluminium that is obtained when a current of $300000\text{ A}$ is passed for 24 hours. Give your answer to **three** significant figures.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why chromium metal cannot be obtained by the electrolysis of dilute aqueous chromium(II) sulfate. Your answer should include data from the *Data Booklet*.
